bib.title: Demonstrate-Search-Predict: Composing retrieval and language models for knowledge-intensive NLP

SOURCE: "Demonstrate–Search–Predict: Composing retrieval and language models for knowledge-intensive NLP", Omar Khattab, Keshav Santhanam, Xiang Lisa Li, David Hall, Percy Liang, Christopher Potts, Matei Zaharia (Stanford). Preprint: the PDF says "Preprint." and is stamped "arXiv:2212.14024v2 [cs.CL] 23 Jan 2023". The PDF names no venue. File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/02-rag-retrieval/sources/khattab-2022-demonstrate-search-predict.pdf

COVERAGE: Read all 73,876 of 73,876 chars (15 pages) with pypdf: body, Table 1, footnotes, conclusion and every reference. There are no appendices. Page numbers below are pypdf pages, counting from 1.

CLAIMS
- claim: Headline result. DSP programs beat the vanilla LM, retrieve-then-read and self-ask by large relative margins.
  number: 37–120% / 8–39% / 80–290%
  setup: Frozen GPT-3.5 text-davinci-002 and frozen ColBERTv2, no fine-tuning. Validation (dev) sets of Open-SQuAD, HotPotQA and QReCC.
  quote: "delivering 37–120%, 8–39%, and 80–290% relative gains against the vanilla LM (GPT-3.5), a standard retrieve-then-read pipeline, and a contemporaneous self-ask pipeline, respectively."
  where: p1 abstract, repeated on p2
  caveat: the 37–120% range does not match the paper's own reported 126% on Open-SQuAD EM (see the next claim and PROBLEMS).
- claim: Table 1 dev results.
  number: Open-SQuAD EM/F1: vanilla 16.2/25.6, retrieve-then-read 33.8/46.1, self-ask 9.3/17.2, DSP 36.6/49.0. HotPotQA EM/F1: vanilla 28.3/36.4, retrieve-then-read 36.9/46.1, self-ask 25.2/33.2 (28.6/37.3 with the refined prompt), DSP 51.4/62.9. QReCC F1/nF1: vanilla 29.8/18.4, retrieve-then-read 31.6/22.2, DSP 35.0/25.3.
  setup: Validation sets subsampled to 1000 questions (400 conversations for QReCC). Average over 5 seeds, each seed with its own 16-shot training set. Each seed covers one fifth of the eval set "To control the language model API spending budget".
  quote: "Retrieve-then-Read 33.8 46.1 36.9 46.1 31.6 22.2" / "Task-aware DSP Program 36.6 49.0 51.4 62.9 35.0 25.3"
  where: p10, Table 1
- claim: On multi-hop HotPotQA, DSP beats the vanilla LM, retrieve-then-read and self-ask by 82%, 39% and 80% relative EM. This is the largest gain over retrieve-then-read, and the authors credit the SEARCH step.
  number: 82% / 39% / 80% EM; 51.4% EM
  setup: HotPotQA fullwiki over the Wikipedia 2017 abstracts corpus. "Hard" examples only. Official validation set used as test. Fixed 2 hops, fusion over n=10 queries per hop, k=5 passages in total.
  quote: "exceeding the vanilla LM, the retrieve-then-read baseline, and the self-ask pipeline by 82%, 39%, and 80%, respectively, in EM. This highlights the effectiveness of building up more sophisticated programs that coordinate the LM and RM for the SEARCH step."
  where: p11
- claim: On single-hop Open-SQuAD the gain over retrieve-then-read is small. The authors credit aggregation across several passages through self-consistency, not multi-hop search.
  number: 126% EM over vanilla; 8% EM and 6% F1 over retrieve-then-read
  setup: Wikipedia Dec 2016. Retrieves k=7 passages with the raw question, then CoT with n=20 reasoning chains and self-consistency.
  quote: "outperforming the vanilla LM baseline by 126% EM relative gains" ... "relative gains of 8% in EM and 6% in F1 over the retrieve-then-read pipeline, highlighting that non-trivial gains are possible by aggregating information across several retrieved passages as we do with self-consistency."
  where: p11
- claim: Self-ask collapses on single-hop questions because of "self-distraction": it decomposes the question tangentially and answers the wrong sub-question.
  number: 9.3% EM
  setup: Self-ask control flow pointed at the same ColBERTv2 index instead of Google Search, Open-SQuAD.
  quote: "the self-ask pipeline, which achieves 9.3% EM, suggesting that its fixed pipeline is ineffective outside its default multi-hop setting... We refer to this behavior of the LM as 'self-distraction'"
  where: p11
- claim: Design argument. The control flow sits in an explicit program, not in the LM's completions. Self-ask "delegates the control flow to the LM completions, maintaining state within the prompt itself".
  number: none
  setup: conceptual argument, §2.4
  quote: "DSP assigns the control flow to an explicit program and facilitates design patterns that invoke the LM (or RM) to conduct small transformations."
  where: p6
- claim: DEMONSTRATE bootstraps demonstrations for the intermediate steps (hop queries, passages) from end-task labels alone. It runs the pipeline zero-shot on training examples and keeps the traces whose answer is correct.
  number: none
  setup: requires the LM and RM to solve at least one or two examples zero-shot
  quote: "If LM and RM can accurately process such transformations 'zero-shot' (i.e., without demonstrations) on at least one or two examples, these examples can be discovered with end-task labels and used as demonstrations."
  where: p4
- claim: The DSP result on Open-SQuAD is comparable to fine-tuned Fusion-in-Decoder base reading 5 passages. FiD reaches 48% when it reads 100 passages.
  number: DPR 29.8% EM (test); FiD about 36% (5 passages) and 48% EM (100 passages)
  setup: Open-SQuAD dev, except DPR, which is a test-set figure
  quote: "on the Open-SQuAD test set, DPR achieves 29.8% EM, well below our 16-shot DSP program... with the default setting of reading 100 passages, their system reaches 48% EM"
  where: p11
- claim: Prior HotPotQA in-context results, including ReAct, trail DSP. These are not apples-to-apples comparisons.
  number: ReAct 35.1% EM; PaLM-540B self-consistency 33.8 EM / 44.6 F1
  setup: different evaluation settings, as the authors concede
  quote: "Yao et al. (2022) achieve 35.1% EM using a system capable of searching using a Wikipedia API. All of these approaches trail our task-aware DSP program, which achieves 51.4% EM"
  where: p11
- claim: The context window limits how many demonstrations fit.
  number: 4097 tokens; 3–5 demos
  setup: text-davinci-002
  quote: "GPT-3.5 text-davinci-002 has a context window of 4097 tokens, which we find to be reasonably large for accommodating several (e.g., 3–5) demonstrations"
  where: p8

COST: The paper reports no LM-call counts, token counts, latency or dollar cost for any system. The only cost statement is the per-seed subsampling "To control the language model API spending budget" (p9). You can infer from the stated configurations that DSP is far more expensive than retrieve-then-read: n=20 sampled chains for Open-SQuAD, n=10 generated queries per hop over 2 hops plus a QA call for HotPotQA, n=10 rewrites for QReCC, and bootstrapping runs in DEMONSTRATE. That is an inference from the configurations. The paper never states it, so do not cite it as a measured number.

LIMITS:
- Results are on dev sets only. Held-out test sets (Open-NQ, FEVER) are promised "in a future version of this report" (p9). "Future versions of this report will include additional test tasks and LM choices." (p2)
- One LM (text-davinci-002, now deprecated) and one retriever. Results are dated.
- There are no ablations. The gain is never broken down into multi-hop search, fusion, self-consistency and bootstrapped demos. The Open-SQuAD gain is attributed to self-consistency without isolating it.
- Five seeds are run, but no variance or confidence intervals are reported.
- Baselines are uneven. Retrieve-then-read uses k=1 passage (2 for multi-hop) and no CoT or self-consistency, while DSP uses k=7 with 20 chains. Self-ask was not evaluated on QReCC.
- The ¶ rows in Table 1 "are not generally apples-to-apples comparisons" (p10).
- The `branch`, `knn` and `crossval` primitives "are currently work-in-progress" (footnote, p8). So the pipelines-of-transformations and adaptive-selection ideas in §2 were not evaluated.
- QReCC was filtered heuristically (conversations containing "other interesting" or "else" were removed) and the authors used it "for developing the DSP abstractions" (p9). Dev-set tuning on the same data the abstractions were built against is a risk.

BUILDS ON: retrieve-then-read: Lee et al. 2019, Khattab et al. 2021b, Lazaridou et al. 2022, Izacard et al. 2022. Multi-hop retrieval: Baleen (Khattab et al. 2021a), IRRR (Qi et al. 2020), Xiong et al. 2020. Self-ask: Press et al. 2022. ColBERT/ColBERTv2: Khattab & Zaharia 2020, Santhanam et al. 2022b. Self-generated rationales: STaR (Zelikman et al. 2022), Wei et al. 2022, Auto-CoT (Zhang et al. 2022), Huang et al. 2022. Self-consistency: Wang et al. 2022c. CombSUM fusion: Fox & Shaw 1994. Gao et al. 2022 (RARR). LM cascades: Dohan et al. 2022. kNN demos: Liu et al. 2021. Cross-validation: Perez et al. 2021. ReAct: Yao et al. 2022. Query rewriting: Anantha et al. 2020.

CODE: the multi-hop SEARCH loop (p6, §2.4), verbatim apart from extraction spacing. Line 10 compares against the string 'N/A'; the extraction garbles the quote marks.
```python
def multihop_search_v2(x, max_hops=3):
    x.hops = []
    for hop in range(max_hops):
        summary, query = generate(hop_template)(x)
        x.hops.append((summary, query))
        if query == 'N/A': break
        passages = retrieve(query, k=5)
        x.context = [summary] + passages
    return x
```
The retrieve-then-read baseline (p9):
```python
def retrieve_then_read_QA(question: str) -> str:
    demos = sample(train, k=16)
    passages = retrieve(question, k=1)
    x = Example(question=question, passages=passages, demos=demos)
    return generate(qa_template)(x).pred
```

FIGURES:
- Figure 1, p1: "A comparison between three systems based on GPT-3.5 (text-davinci-002). On its own, the LM often makes false assertions. An increasingly popular retrieve-then-read pipeline fails when simple search can't find an answer. In contrast, a task-aware DSP program successfully decomposes the problem and produces a correct response." This is the best candidate for the Agentic RAG section. One question ("How many storeys are in the castle David Gregory inherited?") goes through the vanilla LM (invents a castle), retrieve-then-read (retrieves the St. Gregory Hotel) and two-hop search (Kinnairdy Castle, five storeys). It shows the multi-hop failure mode in one picture.
- Figure 2, p2: the three stages of a toy DSP program for multi-hop QA, shown as code with the traces it produces. It is useful for showing how demonstrations are bootstrapped, but it is denser than Figure 1.

PROBLEMS:
- The abstract's "37–120%" gain over the vanilla LM conflicts with the body's "126% EM" on Open-SQuAD. 36.6/16.2 works out to +126%, so the abstract range appears to be stale or computed on a different metric. Quote the per-dataset numbers rather than the range.
- The other headline ranges are consistent with Table 1: HotPotQA 51.4/36.9 is +39%, and Open-SQuAD 36.6/9.3 is about +294%.
- Code listings come out with broken spacing and garbled quote glyphs ("/quotesingle.Var"). They are reconstructed above.
- The PDF contains no embedded instructions.
